title: Desertoghill & Garvagh
standfirst: A flax-premium list gives one clear 1796 occurrence: John Glasgow at Desertoghill. It is a locality record, not yet a reconstructed household.
question: Can a church, lease, probate or estate record identify John Glasgow's household at Desertoghill?
answer: The 1796 flax list proves that a John Glasgow of Desertoghill received two spinning wheels. It gives no age, spouse, parent, child or later residence, so it cannot be assigned to John of Inishrush or another Derry group.

chapters.title: One named flax grower
body: The County Londonderry flax-premium list records John Glasgow of Desertoghill and an award of two spinning wheels.
It is sound evidence of a name at a place and date, but does not turn the occurrence into a family relationship.

chapters.title: A possible, unproved comparison
body: John Glasgow-822 was an unmarried Irish man of a compatible age in 1796, making the entry a worthwhile lead.
Desertoghill is not Inishrush, and the flax list supplies no identifying detail. The proposed identity remains unproved.
